Project Narrative: The proposed project will incorporate bridge lighting across the US 331 Clyde B Wells Bridge in Walton County, FL. This project has been designed by an FDOT Consultant with design funds being allocated through a State legislative appropriation.

The proposed project consists of paving an existing county-maintained dirt roadway to improve the overall safety, reliability, and efficiency of the county’s transportation network. The roadway currently serves local residents, school bus traffic, emergency service providers, and other daily users; however, its unpaved condition creates ongoing maintenance challenges, reduced travel reliability, and hazardous driving conditions during periods of heavy rainfall and dry weather. The project will include roadway grading and shaping, installation or improvement of drainage infrastructure as needed, placement of a stabilized base course, and construction of an asphalt pavement surface. Associated work may also include shoulder improvements, traffic control devices, roadway striping, and erosion control measures necessary to provide a durable and safe transportation corridor. Paving this roadway will provide significant long-term benefits to the county and the traveling public. The project will improve vehicle safety by reducing loose aggregate, washboarding, rutting, dust generation, and muddy conditions that are commonly associated with dirt roads. The improved surface will enhance traction and visibility while reducing the likelihood of accidents and roadway failures during adverse weather conditions. The project will also improve emergency response access and reliability for law enforcement, fire rescue, and medical personnel by providing a dependable all-weather route. School bus operations and daily commuting conditions for residents will be improved through smoother travel surfaces, reduced vehicle wear and tear, and shorter travel times.

From an operational standpoint, paving the roadway will reduce the county’s recurring maintenance costs associated with grading, reshaping, dust suppression, and storm-related repairs that are routinely required on unpaved roads. The paved surface will provide a longer-lasting transportation asset that can be maintained more efficiently and economically over time. In addition, the project will support continued growth and economic development within the county by improving connectivity between residential areas, agricultural properties, local businesses, and other public infrastructure. The upgraded roadway will strengthen the county transportation system by providing safer and more dependable access for residents and visitors while enhancing the overall quality of life for the surrounding community.

Funding Source:
The proposed funding source for the Design phase (FY 27) will be with in-house engineering staff. The budgeted amount of $600,000 would be the anticipated cost for outsourcing of the project.

The proposed funding source for the Construction phase (FY 31) has yet to be determined but staff will continue to evaluate any applicable and appropriate grant sources that may be available to either partially or fully fund this project.

Budget Project Name(s): Chat Holley & US 331 Intersection Improvements (Long Term Option)
Funding Source:
The proposed funding source for the Design phase (FY 27) will be the Capital Projects Fund.  Engineering staff did submit a CIGP application to the Florida Department of Transportation for consideration for financial assistance for this project in March 2026.  FDOT does not typically announce their draft Five Year Work Plan, which would include grant funded projects, until November/December of each year.  It should be noted that the CIGP grant does require a match from the County.  Therefore, in the event of grant award, the County would still have to provide matching funds for the project. 

The proposed funding source for the Construction phase (FY 29) has yet to be determined but staff will continue to evaluate any applicable and appropriate grant sources that may be available to either partially or fully fund this project.
Pertinent Information: The County's Consultant, DRMP, did provide an intersection evaluation report in July 2023 that recommended both short term and long term improvements to the intersection.  County staff and in-house crews have implemented the short term improvements.
Project Narrative: This project proposes intersection improvements to include the installation of luminaries on nearby power poles, construction of a southbound right turn lane on US 331, modification of the existing eastbound right turn lane island and radius on Chat Holley Rd, construction of a dedicated eastbound left turn lane on Chat Holley rd and any other slight realignment to existing southbound travel lanes (south of the intersection) to support the aforementioned intersection modifications.  This project will be constructed within existing County and FDOT right-of-way.

Overlaying the existing asphalt roadway surface will preserve and extend the service life of the County’s transportation infrastructure while improving overall roadway conditions for the traveling public. The project will consist of resurfacing the existing asphalt pavement to address surface deterioration, rutting, cracking, and other deficiencies caused by age, weather, and continuous traffic loading. By correcting surface defects and sealing the existing pavement, the project will also reduce water infiltration into the roadway base, helping to prevent accelerated pavement failure and reducing long-term maintenance costs for the County.

Budget Project Name(s): Hewett Bayou Connector Rd (E Lamb Drive Extension)
Funding Source:
The proposed funding source for the Construction phase was split into two years (FY 26 and FY 27).
 • The amount funded from the FY 26 Capital Projects Fund was $4,271,415.
 • The amount requested from the FY 27 Capital Projects Fund is $4,571,536.

Applications for grant assistance have been submitted to FDOT over multiple years/cycles but was not funded. Previously, the design was funded by FDOT. Due to the timeframe/expiration of the project permits (State and Federal), this project is recommended to move forward with funds programmed by the Capital projects Fund.
Pertinent Information:
County Incentive Grant Program (CIGP) applied in February 2025 $3,971,415 and Capital Infrastructure Fund $3,971,415.

Also, CIGP applied for in March 2024 without award. Again in February 2025 without award.

Total Project Cost for Construction/CEI/Mitigation = $8,842,951
Project Narrative:
This project is for the construction of a new two (2) lane roadway from East Lamb Drive to East Hewett Rd. Scope of work includes the construction of an approximate 325 ft concrete bridge over Hewett Bayou, attached 6 ft sidewalk and associated drainage features. Roadway segment is one (1) mile in length and will be constructed within existing 66 ft County/Public right-of-way. Mitigation costs for permitting is included in the overall project budget.

This project is part of a phased approach to create an alternative roadway connection to US Hwy 98 and expand the transportation network system in an effort to provide alternate routes, improve safety response time for emergency vehicles, alleviate congested roadways, enhance transportation route redundancy, and improve mobility options in the area. The project design was previously funded by FDOT's CIGP program. Due to the construction cost as well as for seeking grant funding opportunities, County staff budgeted approximately 50% of the project cost in FY 26 Capital Projects Fund and the remainder of the project cost is requested as part of FY 27 Capital Projects Fund.

The paved surface will provide a longer-lasting transportation asset that can be maintained more efficiently and economically over time. In addition, the project will support continued growth and economic development within the county by improving connectivity between residential areas, agricultural properties, local businesses, and other public infrastructure. The upgraded roadway will strengthen the county transportation system by providing safer and more dependable access for residents and visitors while enhancing the overall quality of life for the surrounding community.

Project Narrative: The Old Town of Santa Rosa Regional Stormwater Management and Event Facility project is a master-planned development of approximately 220 acres of County-owned property in South Walton. The project is designed to provide regional stormwater management to improve water quality within the Choctawhatchee Bay watershed while also creating public recreational and community amenities. Planned improvements include regional stormwater facilities, an event venue, passive recreational areas, roadway and pedestrian infrastructure, and other supporting site improvements. The project is being developed in phases, with Phase I including the Nellie Drive Extension to provide a new roadway connection through the property.
